The 45th running of the Hotter'N Hell bicycle event in Wichita Falls is on the books.
Event Chairman David Coleman called the four-day event a "rousing success."
"I've talked to so many people that have just raved about how much fun it was," he said.

Coleman said the total number of event participants was 7,824, which was more than the previous year.
The event lived up to its name.
Although the temperature was a pleasant 73 degrees when Saturday's 100-mile Endurance Ride kicked off, it climbed to 105 degrees by 4 p.m., according to the National Weather Service.
Because of the heat, Hell's gate at Burkburnett closed at 11:45 a.m., meaning riders who had not yet reached it were diverted to a shorter 75-mile course.
Coleman said a few people complained, but the course was shortened for health and safety as the full heat of the day arrived.
Coleman also said event planners raised the number of SAG wagons to 50. The support and gear wagons carry water and other supplies for the cyclists. He said the wagons helped about 500 riders.
He said medical personnel attended "a couple of broken bones," but there were no serious medical issues.
A media release from the city of Wichita Falls said 94 riders were treated, and six were hospitalized.
The Endurance Ride was a featured event among several activities offered to participants beginning Thursday in this year's HHH from trail running and rides to kids races to a consumer show.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. (WBTV) - Autumn arrives in just three weeks, but Mother Nature has other ideas for the Carolinas to start the month of September.
A five-day stretch of near-record high temperatures will carry us all the way into the start of Labor Day weekend.
First Alert: Hot weather returns
High temperatures will reach the mid to upper 90s Tuesday through Saturday, and feels-like temperatures will top out between 100-104 degrees. A slight decrease in humidity each afternoon should keep Charlotte barely short of heat advisory criteria but it will be a close call.
Overnight low temperatures will also be very warm, only dropping to the mid-70s. We’ll be close to both record high temperatures and record-warm low temperatures through Saturday.
If you’ll be spending time outdoors, be sure to stay hydrated, take frequent breaks, and avoid prolonged exposure to the afternoon heat. Make sure pets have a cool place to rest and access to fresh water.
Unsettled weekend forecast

CINCINNATI -- Monday's series opener between the Reds and Padres was delayed for several minutes before the start of the fifth inning after home-plate umpire Manny Gonzalez appeared to have medical distress.
According to MLB umpire supervisor Randy Marsh, Gonzalez left due to heat exhaustion. It was a hot and muggy evening in Cincinnati, with first-pitch temperatures officially at 90 degrees at Great American Ball Park.
According to Mike Petraglia on X, Gonzalez received treatment for elevated blood pressure and dehydration. Gonzalez's blood pressure has been restored to normal levels and he is resting comfortably.
As the Reds took the field for the top of the fifth, Gonzalez appeared to be having trouble. Third-base umpire Tom Hanahan came over, followed by Reds head trainer Sean McQueeney and members of the Reds' and Padres' medical staffs.
Soon, Gonzalez took a seat on the grass as he was being evaluated. A medical cart was requested, but he was eventually able to get up and walk off the field with Reds assistant trainer Tomas Vera.
The game resumed after a 14-minute delay with the three remaining umpires on the field. First-base umpire D.J. Reyburn took over for Gonzalez behind the plate. Gonzalez, now in his 14th season, was promoted to the Major League staff for the 2013 season, and he became the first full-time MLB umpire from Venezuela. He has worked in five postseason series, as well as the 2017 All-Star Game.

The warning period runs from 9.00 pm on Tuesday until 6.00 am on Wednesday. However, conditions may also be dangerous on the coasts of the Canary Islands before and after this specific wave warning. The authorities therefore urge people to exercise caution even beyond these locations and times.
Although the weather conditions were the only factor to trigger an alert level, the Aemet has nevertheless issued further warnings for the Canary Islands: Calima, heat and wind at the start of September have kept meteorologists busy alongside the rough seas along the coasts. Rough seas and Calima in the Canary Islands
Whilst the waves are set to fall below the threshold for a warning as early as Wednesday morning, the authorities are still expecting rough seas. This is being caused, amongst other things, by the Calima, which has been sweeping in since Monday.
According to the forecast, the sandstorm carrying fine dust particles from the Sahara – just a few hundred kilometres away – is set to affect the Canary Islands throughout the week. On Tuesday, largely clear skies are expected in the east and light cloud cover in the west of the Canary Islands.
According to Aemet, cloud cover will increase in places from Wednesday, meaning that rain is possible in the north-east of the Canary Islands from Thursday. Thick clouds are expected over Lanzarote. On Friday, the sky is set to be grey, particularly over the central islands. Rain is possible in the south of Tenerife. Light showers are also forecast elsewhere. As the weekend approaches, meteorologists expect the weather to move westwards.

full_text:
September marks the start of meteorological "fall" (Sept. 1 to Nov. 30), but Mother Nature has other plans.
Our hottest stretch since around the Fourth of July is expected through this week leading up to the Labor Day weekend.
Hottest stretch since around the 4th of July
Temperatures on this Monday reached 90 to 95 degrees in spite of some morning clouds, and the humidity made it feel close to 100 degrees.
As a ridge of high pressure in the Midwest shifts east our temperatures will only climb in the coming days.
A heat advisory is in effect Tuesday into Wednesday for the Scioto Valley, and much of the rest of the area will likely end up under a heat advisory by Wednesday and Thursday.
Temperatures each day will reach the mid to upper 90s from Tuesday to Friday and the humidity will push our heat index over 100. The hottest days appear to be Wednesday and Thursday when the heat index could reach 105 degrees or higher.
High temps and heat index this week
Record highs are from the Dust Bowl decade (1930s) and are mostly 100 or higher. While our heat index will reach that number at times the air temperature likely stays a few degrees below.
Record highs from the Dust Bowl (1930s) look safe this week
Definitely take frequent breaks if you have to work outdoors or delay it until late afternoon or evening when the sun angle is weaker. Some practice times may need to be rearranged to other times of the day when heat isn't as bad.
That ridge will generally lead to dry weather locally as strong storm clusters stay near and north of Interstate 70 into eastern Ohio, Pennsylvania and the northeast. However, by the end of the week the ridge will begin to weaken as a cold front presses south.
Labor Day weekend features a southward moving cold front
Our storm chances will increase Friday and Saturday although exact timing and coverage remains to be determined.
It's certainly possible we could have some lightning delays for some high school football games Friday and perhaps even one for the Mountaineer home opener Saturday. We'll keep you updated.
Mountaineers may see a shower/storm nearby at some point Saturday
Temps will slowly back down this weekend as the front pushes south and by Labor Day Monday we should be back to average temperatures (mid 80s) with only spotty shower/storm chances.
